cues.en: What do you think is the key to achieving our goals, our success?
cues.zh: 你认为实现目标、取得成功的关键是什么？

cues.en: Some people suggest things like hard work,
cues.zh: 有人会说是努力工作、

cues.en: focus, persistence.
cues.zh: 专注、坚持。

cues.en: But research shows these are all byproducts of something else, something much more powerful that we can all develop.
cues.zh: 但研究表明，这些都只是另一种东西的副产品，而那样东西要强大得多，而且我们每个人都能培养。

cues.en: It is this very special something that really is critical to success, and it's what I'm here to discuss with you today.
cues.zh: 正是这个特别的东西，才是成功真正的关键，也是我今天想和大家讨论的。

cues.en: Someone who has achieved great success is Josh Waidskin,
cues.zh: 有一位取得巨大成功的人，叫 Josh Waidskin，

cues.en: a chess international master and the subject of the movie
cues.zh: 他是国际象棋国际大师，也是电影

cues.en: Searching for Bobby Fischer.
cues.zh: 《寻找鲍比·菲舍尔》的原型人物。

cues.en: Nobody has won all the national chess championships that Josh has.
cues.zh: 没有人像 Josh 那样赢下过所有全国国际象棋锦标赛冠军。

cues.en: But even more impressive, when he turned 21,
cues.zh: 但更令人惊叹的是，他满 21 岁时，

cues.en: he took on the challenge of mastering something completely new and very different from chess,
cues.zh: 他接受了挑战，去掌握一种与象棋完全不同、全新的东西，

cues.en: martial arts.
cues.zh: 武术。

cues.en: He realized
cues.zh: 他意识到

cues.en: that he had learned how to grow and succeed, and he could apply that understanding to other domains.
cues.zh: 自己已经学会了如何成长和成功，并且能把这种理解应用到其他领域。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 于是，

cues.en: he devoted himself relentlessly to Tai Chi Chuan.
cues.zh: 他坚持不懈地投入太极拳。

cues.en: And after lots of hard work, many failures,
cues.zh: 经过大量努力、许多失败，

cues.en: and some broken joints,
cues.zh: 还有一些关节损伤，

cues.en: he became a great martial artist and he won two world championships.
cues.zh: 他成为了一位伟大的武术家，并赢得了两次世界冠军。

cues.en: Now he's off to jujitsu.
cues.zh: 现在他要去练柔术了。

cues.en: So what does Josh say is the greatest thing that ever happened to him?
cues.zh: 那 Josh 说，他人生中最棒的事是什么？

cues.en: Believe it or not, he says,
cues.zh: 信不信由你，他说是——

cues.en: losing my first national chess championship
cues.zh: 输掉我的第一场全国国际象棋锦标赛

cues.en: because it helped me avoid many of the psychological traps.
cues.zh: 因为这帮我避开了许多心理陷阱。

cues.en: The key trap that Josh avoided
cues.zh: Josh 避开的关键陷阱

cues.en: was believing that he was special, that he was smarter than other people, and that he didn't have to work hard.
cues.zh: 就是认为自己很特别、比别人聪明，觉得自己不必努力。

cues.en: He could have thought of himself as a prodigy,
cues.zh: 他本可以把自己当成神童，

cues.en: but he doesn't think that he has extraordinary intelligence.
cues.zh: 但他并不认为自己智力超群。

cues.en: He says,
cues.zh: 他说，

cues.en: the moment we believe that success is determined by an ingrained level of ability,
cues.zh: 一旦我们相信成功由根深蒂固的能力水平决定，

cues.en: we will be brittle in the face of adversity.
cues.zh: 我们在逆境面前就会变得脆弱。

cues.en: Josh often quotes Stanford professor, Carol Dweck,
cues.zh: Josh 经常引用斯坦福教授 Carol Dweck 的话，

cues.en: who discovered that some people see intelligence or abilities as fixed, what is called a fixed mindset,
cues.zh: 她发现，有些人认为智力或能力是固定的，这被称为固定型思维，

cues.en: while other people see them, as Josh does, as qualities that can be developed,
cues.zh: 而另一些人则像 Josh 一样，把它们看作可以发展的品质，

cues.en: a growth mindset.
cues.zh: 也就是成长型思维。

cues.en: More important,
cues.zh: 更重要的是，

cues.en: doctor Dweck discovered that these two different mindsets lead to very different behaviors and results.
cues.zh: Dweck 博士发现，这两种不同的思维模式会导致截然不同的行为和结果。

cues.en: In a study she did with doctor Lisa Blackwell,
cues.zh: 她与 Lisa Blackwell 医生做了一项研究，

cues.en: several hundred seventh graders were surveyed to determine which mindset each student had, and then they were tracked for two years.
cues.zh: 调查了几百名七年级学生，判断每个人持哪种思维模式，然后跟踪了他们两年。

cues.en: Results showed that the students with a growth mindset,
cues.zh: 结果显示，具有成长型思维的学生，

cues.en: those who thought they could change their own intelligence,
cues.zh: 也就是那些认为自己能改变自身智力的人，

cues.en: increased their grades over time,
cues.zh: 成绩随时间提高了，

cues.en: while those with a fixed mindset did not.
cues.zh: 而固定型思维的学生没有。

cues.en: You can see the trend. The gap in performance just widens and widens over time.
cues.zh: 你能看到这个趋势：表现差距只会随时间越拉越大。

cues.en: The difference between these two groups?
cues.zh: 这两组人的区别是什么？

cues.en: A different perspective on intelligence.
cues.zh: 从不同视角看智力。

cues.en: Other studies have shown similar effects for our mindset about other abilities,
cues.zh: 其他研究表明，我们对自己其他能力的思维模式也有类似影响，

cues.en: like problem solving, playing sports, managing people, or anything else you'd like. Dancing la macarena.
cues.zh: 比如解决问题、做运动、管理他人，或者任何你想做的事。跳《Macarena》舞。

cues.en: The key to success
cues.zh: 成功的关键

cues.en: is not simply effort or focus or resilience, but it is the growth mindset that creates them. The mindset itself is critical.
cues.zh: 不只是努力、专注或韧性，而是创造这些的成长型思维。思维模式本身至关重要。

cues.en: Research shows that when we directly try to build grit or persistence,
cues.zh: 研究表明，当我们直接尝试培养坚毅或坚持时，

cues.en: it is not nearly as effective as addressing the mindset that underlies them.
cues.zh: 其效果远不如去改变支撑它们的思维方式。

cues.en: How many of us think of ourselves as not math people, or creative,
cues.zh: 我们中有多少人认为自己不是学数学的料，或者不擅长创造，

cues.en: or sociable, or athletic,
cues.zh: 或不善社交，或不擅长运动，

cues.en: or conversely,
cues.zh: 或者反过来，

cues.en: that we're naturals?
cues.zh: 认为自己是天生的？

cues.en: If we're to fulfill our potential,
cues.zh: 如果我们要发挥自己的潜力，

cues.en: we have to start thinking differently.
cues.zh: 就必须开始换一种思考方式。

cues.en: We have to realize that our... We're not chained to our current capabilities.
cues.zh: 我们必须认识到，我们的……我们并不受限于当前的能力。

cues.en: Neuroscience shows that the brain is very malleable, and we can change our own ability to think and to perform.
cues.zh: 神经科学研究表明，大脑具有极强的可塑性，我们能够改变自己的思维能力和表现水平。

cues.en: In fact,
cues.zh: 事实上，

cues.en: many of the most accomplished people of our era were thought of by experts to have no future.
cues.zh: 我们这个时代许多最有成就的人，曾被专家认定没有前途。

cues.en: People like Charles Darwin, Lucille Ball, Marcel Proust, and many others.
cues.zh: 比如查尔斯·达尔文、露西尔·鲍尔、马塞尔·普鲁斯特，以及许多其他人。

cues.en: But they, along with all great achievers,
cues.zh: 但他们和所有伟大的成就者一样，

cues.en: from Mozart to Einstein,
cues.zh: 从莫扎特到爱因斯坦，

cues.en: built their abilities.
cues.zh: 都是靠后天培养出能力的。

cues.en: But the key insight that I would like you to walk away with today is that when we realize that, when we realize that we can change our own abilities, when we have a growth mindset, we bring our game to new levels.
cues.zh: 但我希望大家今天能带走的关键洞见是：当我们意识到这一点，当我们意识到自己能够改变自身能力，当我们拥有成长型思维时，我们就能把表现提升到新的高度。

cues.en: So how does a growth mindset do that?
cues.zh: 那么成长型思维是如何做到这一点的？

cues.en: It turns out that there are physiological manifestations to mindset.
cues.zh: 原来，思维模式在生理上是有体现的。

cues.en: Brain scans show that for people with a fixed mindset, the brain becomes most active when receiving information about how the person performed, such as a grade or a score.
cues.zh: 脑部扫描显示，对于固定型思维的人，大脑在接收关于自己表现的信息时最活跃，比如成绩或分数。

cues.en: But for people with a growth mindset, the brain becomes most active when receiving information about what they could do better next time.
cues.zh: 但对成长型思维的人来说，大脑在接收关于下次如何做得更好的信息时最活跃。

cues.en: In other words, people with a fixed mindset worry the most about how they're judged, while those with a growth mindset focus the most on learning.
cues.zh: 换句话说，固定型思维的人最担心别人怎么评价自己，而成长型思维的人最关注学习。

cues.en: There are other consequences of mindset. People with a fixed mindset see effort as a bad thing, something that only people with low capabilities need, while those with a growth mindset see effort as what makes us smart, as the way to grow.
cues.zh: 思维方式还有其他影响。固定型思维的人把努力看成坏事，认为只有能力低的人才需要努力；成长型思维的人则把努力看作让人变聪明、获得成长的方式。

cues.en: And when they hit a setback or failure,
cues.zh: 而当他们遇到挫折或失败时，

cues.en: people with a fixed mindset tend to conclude that they're incapable. So to protect their ego,
cues.zh: 固定型思维的人往往会认定自己能力不行。于是为了保护自尊，

cues.en: they lose interest or withdraw.
cues.zh: 他们就会失去兴趣或选择退缩。

cues.en: We observe that as lack of motivation,
cues.zh: 我们看到这像是缺乏动力，

cues.en: but behind it is a fixed mindset.
cues.zh: 但背后其实是固定型思维。

cues.en: Whereas people with a growth mindset understand that setbacks are part of growth. So when they hit one, they find a way around it like Josh Wadeskin did when he lost in chess or in martial arts.
cues.zh: 而拥有成长型思维的人明白，挫折是成长的一部分。所以遇到挫折时，他们会想办法绕过它，就像 Josh Wadeskin 在国际象棋或武术中失利时那样。

cues.en: Research clearly shows these effects of mindset.
cues.zh: 研究清楚地显示了思维模式的这些影响。

cues.en: In one study that doctor Dweck did with doctor Claudia Mueller, they had children do a set of puzzles,
cues.zh: 在 Dweck 博士与 Claudia Mueller 博士合作的一项研究中，他们让孩子们做一组拼图，

cues.en: and then they praised the kids.
cues.zh: 然后表扬了这些孩子。

cues.en: To some of the kids, they said, wow, that's a really good score. You must be smart at this.
cues.zh: 对其中一些孩子，他们说，哇，这个分数真不错。你一定很聪明。

cues.en: That's fixed mindset praise because it portrays intelligence
cues.zh: 这是固定型思维的表扬，因为它把智力

cues.en: or abilities as a fixed quality.
cues.zh: 或能力说成是一种固定的特质。

cues.en: To other kids, said,
cues.zh: 对另一些孩子，他们说，

cues.en: that's a really good score. You must have tried really hard.
cues.zh: 这个分数真不错。你一定很努力。

cues.en: That's growth mindset praise because it focuses on the process.
cues.zh: 这是成长型思维的表扬，因为它关注的是过程。

cues.en: Then they asked the kids, okay, what kind of puzzle would you like to do next? An easy one or a hard one?
cues.zh: 然后他们问孩子，好，接下来你想做哪种题？简单的还是难的？

cues.en: The majority of the kids who received the fixed mindset praise chose to do the easy puzzle, while the great majority of those who received the growth mindset praise chose to challenge themselves.
cues.zh: 大多数被表扬“固定型思维”的孩子选择了简单的拼图，而绝大多数被表扬“成长型思维”的孩子选择了挑战自己。

cues.en: Then all the re... Then the researchers gave a hard puzzle to all of the kids because they were interested in seeing what confronting difficulty would do to their performance.
cues.zh: 然后所有……然后研究人员给所有孩子一个很难的拼图，因为他们想看看面对困难会如何影响他们的表现。

cues.en: Look at what happened when the kids later went back to the set of easier problems that they started with.
cues.zh: 看看孩子们后来回到一开始那组较简单的拼图时发生了什么。

cues.en: The kids who received the fixed mindset praise did significantly worse than they had originally,
cues.zh: 接受固定型思维夸奖的孩子，表现明显比原先差，

cues.en: while those who received the growth mindset praise did better.
cues.zh: 而接受成长型思维夸奖的孩子则表现更好。

cues.en: And to top it off,
cues.zh: 更糟的是，

cues.en: at the very end, kids were asked to report their scores.
cues.zh: 最后，孩子们被要求报告自己的分数。

cues.en: And the kids who received the fixed mindset praise lied about their scores over three times more often than those who received the growth praise. They did not have another way to cope with their failure.
cues.zh: 接受固定型思维夸奖的孩子谎报分数的次数，是接受成长型夸奖孩子的三倍多。他们没有别的办法来应对失败。

cues.en: The difference between these two groups, one short little sentence.
cues.zh: 这两组人的区别，可以用一句简短的话概括。

cues.en: How often
cues.zh: 我们有多经常

cues.en: do we praise kids for being smart or for being great at something?
cues.zh: 表扬孩子聪明，或者表扬他们擅长某件事？

cues.en: We've been told that this will raise their self esteem,
cues.zh: 我们一直被告知，这会提升他们的自尊心，

cues.en: but instead,
cues.zh: 但结果却相反，

cues.en: it puts them in a fixed mindset. They become afraid of challenges and they lose confidence when things hit hard.
cues.zh: 这会让他们形成固定型思维。他们会害怕挑战，遇到困难时也会失去信心。

cues.en: As Josh Waidskins says,
cues.zh: 正如 Josh Waidskins 所说，

cues.en: it is incredibly important for parents to make their feedback process related as opposed to praising or criticizing talent.
cues.zh: 父母让反馈与过程相关，而不是表扬或批评天赋，这一点极其重要。

cues.en: If we win because we're a winner, then when we lose, it must make us a loser.
cues.zh: 如果我们赢了，是因为我们天生就是赢家，那么一旦输了，就一定说明我们是输家。

cues.en: These studies show not only the mechanisms by which mindset affects performance,
cues.zh: 这些研究不仅揭示了心态影响表现的机制，

cues.en: but they also show something else that's very important.
cues.zh: 还揭示了另一件非常重要的事。

cues.en: They show that we can change mindsets,
cues.zh: 它们表明，心态是可以改变的，

cues.en: and that's important because most of us have fixed mindsets about something.
cues.zh: 这很重要，因为我们大多数人在某些方面都有固定型心态。

cues.en: Another study that showed that we can change mindsets is one in which Dweck and Blackwell
cues.zh: 另一项证明心态可以改变的研究，是 Dweck 和 Blackwell

cues.en: did a workshop with seventh graders to instill a growth mindset in them.
cues.zh: 为七年级学生举办工作坊，培养他们的成长型心态。

cues.en: As a result of the workshop, the students gained more interest in learning and they worked harder. And as a result of that, their grades improved.
cues.zh: 这次工作坊之后，学生对学习更感兴趣了，也更用功了。结果，他们的成绩提高了。

cues.en: Other studies have shown that when we teach a growth mindset, not only does it improve achievement for students as a whole, but it also narrows the achievement gap because the effects are most pronounced for the students who face negative stereotypes,
cues.zh: 其他研究表明，当我们教授成长型思维时，不仅能整体提升学生的成绩，还能缩小成绩差距，因为这种效果对面临负面刻板印象的学生最明显，

cues.en: such as minority students and girls in math.
cues.zh: 比如少数族裔学生和数学科目中的女生。

cues.en: I've spoken mostly about children, but mindset affects all of us.
cues.zh: 我主要谈的是孩子，但心态影响我们所有人。

cues.en: In our workplaces,
cues.zh: 在职场中，

cues.en: managers with fixed mindsets don't welcome feedback as much, and they don't mentor employees as much. And employees with growth mindsets about specific skills like negotiations
cues.zh: 固定型心态的管理者不太欢迎反馈，也不太指导员工。而对谈判等具体技能持成长型心态的员工

cues.en: become far better at those skills than people with fixed views.
cues.zh: 在这些技能上会比持固定观念的人强得多。

cues.en: Mindsets can even help us solve big social issues.
cues.zh: 心态甚至能帮我们解决重大社会问题。

cues.en: A recent study showed that when we expose Israelis and Palestinians to the idea that groups can change,
cues.zh: 最近一项研究表明，当我们让以色列人和巴勒斯坦人接触“群体可以改变”这一观念时，

cues.en: they increase their attitudes toward one another, they improve them,
cues.zh: 他们对彼此的态度会提升、会改善，

cues.en: and they enhance their willingness
cues.zh: 也更愿意

cues.en: to compromise and to work for peace.
cues.zh: 妥协并为和平而努力。

cues.en: We also see the effects of mindset on relationships,
cues.zh: 我们也看到思维模式对人际关系的影响，

cues.en: sports,
cues.zh: 对运动，

cues.en: health.
cues.zh: 对健康的影响。

cues.en: How is it possible that as a society, we're not asking schools to develop a growth mindset in children?
cues.zh: 作为一个社会，我们怎么竟没有要求学校培养孩子的成长型思维？

cues.en: Our myopic efforts to teach them facts,
cues.zh: 我们短视地教他们事实、

cues.en: concepts,
cues.zh: 概念、

cues.en: and even critical thinking skills is likely to fail if we don't also deliberately teach them the essential beliefs that will allow them to succeed, not only in school, but also beyond.
cues.zh: 甚至批判性思维技能，这很可能失败——除非我们还有意教给他们那些能让他们成功的核心信念，不仅在学校，也在学校之外。

cues.en: There's a lot that we can do to change mindsets.
cues.zh: 我们可以做很多事来改变思维模式。

cues.en: But here are three things that any of us can do to instill a growth mindset in ourselves and in those around us.
cues.zh: 但以下三件事，任何一个人都可以做，来在自己和身边人身上培养成长型思维。

cues.en: First,
cues.zh: 第一，

cues.en: recognize that the growth mindset is not only beneficial,
cues.zh: 要认识到，成长型思维不仅有益，

cues.en: but it's also supported by science.
cues.zh: 而且有科学依据。

cues.en: Neuroscience shows that the brain changes and becomes more capable when we work hard to improve ourselves.
cues.zh: 神经科学表明，当我们努力提升自己时，大脑会发生变化，能力也会增强。

cues.en: Second,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: learn and teach others about how to develop our abilities. Learn about deliberate practice and what makes for effective effort.
cues.zh: 学习并教别人如何发展能力：了解刻意练习，以及什么造就了有效的努力。

cues.en: When we understand how to develop our abilities, we strengthen our conviction that we're in charge of them.
cues.zh: 当我们懂得如何发展自己的能力，就会更加坚信自己能掌控这些能力。

cues.en: And third,
cues.zh: 第三，

cues.en: listen for your fixed mindset voice.
cues.zh: 留意你内心的固定型思维声音。

cues.en: And when you hear it,
cues.zh: 当你听到它时，

cues.en: talk back with a growth mindset voice.
cues.zh: 用成长型思维的声音回击它。

cues.en: If you hear,
cues.zh: 如果你听到

cues.en: I can't do it,
cues.zh: “我做不到”，

cues.en: add
cues.zh: 就加上

cues.en: yet.
cues.zh: “还”字。

cues.en: My request to you today
cues.zh: 今天我想请大家

cues.en: is that you share this knowledge about the growth mindset with your family, friends, and schools,
cues.zh: 把关于成长型思维的知识分享给家人、朋友和学校，

cues.en: so that all of us can go and fulfill our potential.
cues.zh: 这样我们所有人都能去发挥自己的潜能。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
